meta.title: Ravi's Badminton Email
meta.textType: functional: an email about a sport, with pictures

paragraphs: On Monday, November twenty-third, Leo and Lily sat at the library computer after school. Lily sat next to him and watched the screen. Leo had a new email from his pen pal Ravi. The subject of the email was "My badminton team." Leo read the first lines out loud. "Dear Leo, thank you for your last email." "Today I want to tell you about my favorite sport."

"I play badminton on Tuesdays and Fridays at the sports center near my school." "I am in the badminton club, and we usually play for two hours." "My team has eight players." "I like riding my bike to the center." "On rainy days, my dad drives me." "The center has a big gym with six courts." "Playing badminton is good exercise, and it helps me get fit." "I am not a fast runner, but I love moving quickly on the court."

"A badminton court is a rectangle with a net across the middle." "Every point starts with a serve from behind the service line." "You hit the shuttlecock over the net with a racket, and the other player hits it back." "You must hit it before it touches the floor." "If the shuttlecock falls on your side, the other player gets a point." "The winner of a game is the first player with twenty-one points."

"Our team played in a school competition last month." "We did not win, but we had fun." "If we practice a lot, we will play better." "I hope that we will win next time." "How often do you play a sport?" "What is your favorite sport, and why do you like it?" "Best wishes, Ravi."

Leo wrote back to Ravi. Lily typed the answer. "Dear Ravi, I play football every Wednesday after school." "My friends and I play on the school field." "Playing football is fun, but I am a slow runner, too." "Please send me a photo of your team." "Best wishes, Leo." At the end, he added a line. "P.S. The ball is faster than me!"
text.summary: Leo and Lily read an email from Leo's pen pal Ravi about badminton. Ravi tells about his team, the court, and the rules, and he asks how often Leo plays a sport. Leo writes back about football.

sentences.text: On Monday, November twenty-third, Leo and Lily sat at the library computer after school.
Lily sat next to him and watched the screen.
Leo had a new email from his pen pal Ravi.
The subject of the email was "My badminton team."
Leo read the first lines out loud.
"Dear Leo, thank you for your last email."
"Today I want to tell you about my favorite sport."
"I play badminton on Tuesdays and Fridays at the sports center near my school."
"I am in the badminton club, and we usually play for two hours."
"My team has eight players."
"I like riding my bike to the center."
"On rainy days, my dad drives me."
"The center has a big gym with six courts."
"Playing badminton is good exercise, and it helps me get fit."
"I am not a fast runner, but I love moving quickly on the court."
"A badminton court is a rectangle with a net across the middle."
"Every point starts with a serve from behind the service line."
"You hit the shuttlecock over the net with a racket, and the other player hits it back."
"You must hit it before it touches the floor."
"If the shuttlecock falls on your side, the other player gets a point."
"The winner of a game is the first player with twenty-one points."
"Our team played in a school competition last month."
"We did not win, but we had fun."
"If we practice a lot, we will play better."
"I hope that we will win next time."
"How often do you play a sport?"
"What is your favorite sport, and why do you like it?"
"Best wishes, Ravi."
Leo wrote back to Ravi.
Lily typed the answer.
"Dear Ravi, I play football every Wednesday after school."
"My friends and I play on the school field."
"Playing football is fun, but I am a slow runner, too."
"Please send me a photo of your team."
"Best wishes, Leo."
At the end, he added a line.
"P.S. The ball is faster than me!"
